general_information.Description: This course is designed based on the Coursera AI for Cybersecurity Specialization by Johns Hopkins University. The course introduces how artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques are applied to cybersecurity problems, including email threat detection, spam and phishing classification, authentication security, malware detection, network anomaly detection, fraud prevention, adversarial machine learning, Generative Adversarial Networks, reinforcement learning, and AI model evaluation. Students learn to frame cybersecurity problems as data-driven AI tasks, engineer security-relevant features, train and evaluate supervised and unsupervised models, analyze anomalies in network traffic, and assess the robustness of AI systems against adversarial conditions. The course emphasizes defensive, ethical, and responsible applications of AI in cybersecurity through Coursera-based videos, readings, quizzes, hands-on notebooks, and review sessions.
general_information.StudentTasks: Student must complete the online learning activities and get the certificate of AI for Cybersecurity Specialization from Coursera to be accepted to the final examination.
general_information.Tools: Coursera, Jupyter Notebook, Python, common machine learning libraries, course datasets and online quizzes/labs.
general_information.Note: 1. Final Exam included Final Theory Exam (TE): 100% 2. Student gets 0.3 bonus points for each course completed on time. The total bonus point is not greater than 1. 3. Completion Criteria: Final TE Score >=4 & (Final TE Score + bonus) >= 5 4. Complete the online courses and get all specialization certifications to be allowed to take Final Exam

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Learners should be able to explain AI-driven cybersecurity use cases, security threat detection workflows, and the machine learning development process for cybersecurity applications.
Learners should be able to develop and evaluate machine learning models for email security, spam/phishing detection, and AI-supported authentication security.
Learners should be able to analyze malware and network traffic features and apply supervised or unsupervised learning algorithms for malware and anomaly detection.
Learners should be able to implement network anomaly detection experiments using botnet or traffic data and interpret model evaluation results for cybersecurity decision-making.
Learners should be able to apply advanced AI security concepts, including fraud detection, GANs, adversarial machine learning, model resilience, and reinforcement learning for adaptive cybersecurity.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All studied courses in AI for Cybersecurity Specialization. Each major topic contributes 4-5 questions: AI for cybersecurity fundamentals, email threat detection, authentication security, malware detection, network anomaly detection, fraud detection, GANs, adversarial ML, reinforcement learning, and model evaluation.
assessments.Note: Customized from the quizzes of this specialization. 1st Evaluation (exam): For students who completed & got Coursera's specialization certificates (Option at week 7); 2nd Evaluation (exam): For students who completed & got Coursera's specialization certificates) at week 13; 3rd Evaluation (re-exam): For students who completed & got Coursera's specialization certificates) at week 14.

constructive_questions.Name: AI for cyber threat detection
constructive_questions.Details: How can AI improve threat detection without replacing the need for human cybersecurity judgment?

constructive_questions.Name: Security data and ML workflow
constructive_questions.Details: What cybersecurity data characteristics make a machine learning model reliable or unreliable?

constructive_questions.Name: Email security classification
constructive_questions.Details: How should a team evaluate whether a spam/phishing classifier is safe enough for deployment?

constructive_questions.Name: AI-supported authentication
constructive_questions.Details: What are the benefits and risks of biometric AI for authentication security?

constructive_questions.Name: Malware feature engineering
constructive_questions.Details: Which malware features are most useful for detection, and how can feature choices introduce bias?

constructive_questions.Name: Malware detection models
constructive_questions.Details: Why might supervised and unsupervised methods produce different malware detection outcomes?

constructive_questions.Name: Network anomaly detection
constructive_questions.Details: What makes an anomaly meaningful in network traffic, and how can false positives be managed?

constructive_questions.Name: Botnet traffic analysis
constructive_questions.Details: How should model results be communicated to support cybersecurity decision-making?

constructive_questions.Name: Fraud detection
constructive_questions.Details: Why is model evaluation especially important when detecting rare fraud events?

constructive_questions.Name: GANs and adversarial AI
constructive_questions.Details: How can synthetic data and adversarial attacks both help and challenge cybersecurity defense?

constructive_questions.Name: Model resilience
constructive_questions.Details: What evidence is needed to claim that an AI security model is robust?

constructive_questions.Name: Responsible AI for cybersecurity
constructive_questions.Details: How can AI cybersecurity systems be designed to be effective, explainable, and ethically defensible?
